bugs.error_message: Panel header showed '! expired' (claiming the usage auth token had died) for ANY poll failure — a dropped connection, an HTTP 5xx, or a parse failure — while the hover tooltip contradicted it with the real cause.
bugs.root_cause: UsagePoller has separate onAuthExpired and onError callbacks, but both wrote into one stringly-typed `usageError: String?`, and usageNotice mapped `usageError != nil` -> "expired". The distinction the poller made was discarded at the boundary. Compounding it, usageError was only cleared by a SUCCESSFUL poll, so turning polling off while an error showed pinned the notice in the header forever.
bugs.fix: Replaced usageError with a `UsageFailure` enum (.authExpired -> "expired", .transient(msg) -> "error"), each owning its own notice word and tooltip detail. stopPolling() now clears usageFailure, since a 'usage isn't refreshing' notice is meaningless once nothing is polling. Test locks the two words apart.

SetupInstaller.swift was added during the first-run-installer work and auto-joined the Xcode target — 'claude spinner/' is a SYNCHRONIZED ROOT GROUP, so new files need no pbxproj edit — but the hand-kept list in run.sh rotted silently behind that. Invisible in practice because a machine with full Xcode always takes the xcodebuild branch; only a CommandLineTools-only machine hits the fallback. bugs.error_message: Self-review finding: removing usageModelId left UsageSnapshot.modelId write-only — still parsed, still carried into the snapshot, still serialised to UserDefaults on every poll, never read.
bugs.root_cause: A dead-code removal that deleted the last READER of a field without checking what fed it. The chain StatusFile.Model.id -> SessionFeed.modelId -> UsageSnapshot.modelId existed solely to serve usageModelId, so removing the tail turned the whole chain into dead weight rather than removing it.
bugs.fix: Removed the chain end to end. Old persisted snapshots still carry a modelId key; JSONDecoder ignores unknown keys, so no migration needed. LESSON: when deleting a dead accessor, grep what WROTE the thing it read, not just what read it.

bugs.error_message: 7d gauge reads as empty below 10% — an 8% bar is indistinguishable from an empty track
bugs.root_cause: UsageGauge dimmed the fill to 35% opacity under 10%, meant to keep a low level from shouting. The track behind it is already secondary at 22% opacity, so the dimmed fill had almost no contrast against it — and 7d sits under 10% most of the week, so the common case was the invisible one.
bugs.fix: Removed the .opacity(pct < 10 ? 0.35 : 1.0) modifier. The tint plus the existing 3pt minimum sliver already keep a low level quiet without erasing it.

bugs.error_message: chg gauge saturates at ≥20 points — +52% and +20% render identical bars
bugs.root_cause: TrendGauge filled linearly over a fullScale of 20 points, so min(fullScale, |delta|)/fullScale pinned at 1.0 for every move past 20. The gauge's whole job is comparing magnitudes and it stopped doing so exactly where the moves get interesting.
bugs.fix: Replaced the linear 20-point scale with sqrt(min(100,|delta|)/100) over the full range, extracted as the pure TrendGauge.fillFraction(delta:). Keeps resolution at single-digit deltas (where samples usually land) and leaves headroom to 100. Three regression tests cover saturation, clamping/sign, and small-delta resolution.

bugs.error_message: Name column truncates (`continue from…`) while the status column beside it sits half empty
bugs.root_cause: The name (105pt) and status (103pt) columns were BOTH fixed, so the division between them was a guess applied to every row regardless of content. 'done' needs 26.5pt and got 103pt while the unbounded name truncated next to it; 'running TodoWrite' needs 112.6pt and overran its 103pt anyway. Same static split, two opposite failures. Third in the bug-111/122 family — all three are a hand-picked column constant that fits some content and not other.
bugs.fix: Added RowLayout.nameWidth(statusLabel:), a pure function that gives the status its measured width (Menlo advance x count + 4pt slack, capped so the name keeps a 70pt floor) and hands the remainder to the name. Idle rows go 15 -> 24 chars of name; every label in the status vocabulary now fits, TodoWrite included. Advance is measured off NSFont rather than estimated at ~0.602 x size (the estimate was accurate to 2dp, so this removes a hand-rederived constant, not a bug). 4 unit tests cover fit, slack handoff, the name floor, and budget conservation.

bugs.error_message: SetupInstaller.copyExecutable deleted and replaced ~/.claude/statusline-command.sh with no backup, silently destroying local edits on every install.
bugs.root_cause: copyExecutable did `if fileExists { removeItem }` then copy. The installer treated the two artefacts asymmetrically: settings.json was backed up to .backup-<epoch> before writing (install():69-82) and its statusLine key was left alone if already set, but the *scripts* were clobbered unconditionally. install() is documented 'Safe to re-run', which was true of settings and false of the scripts. Latent, not theoretical: the installed statusline had drifted far ahead of the bundled copy (truecolor gradient, git branch/dirty, 1M tier, burn-rate ETA, trend/warn/hint glyphs, single-jq extraction) and survived only because nobody had reinstalled.
bugs.fix: copyExecutable now preserves a differing destination as <name>.backup-<epoch> before replacing, reusing the settings.json naming. A byte-identical destination is skipped entirely so re-runs don't accumulate empty backups. Made internal (was private) + injectable `now` so it is testable; three tests exercise it in a temp dir, never against the live ~/.claude. Verified the preservation test bites: reverting to the old body fails it with the backup absent.

bugs.error_message: git add -A swept a concurrent session's in-progress work into an unrelated commit (306e2bf)
bugs.root_cause: Another Claude session (statusline-drift) was working in the same repo. `git add -A` stages the whole worktree, not this session's edits, so SetupInstaller.swift (+34) and 67 lines of their tests landed in a commit whose message was about panel verification. Second time in this session lineage that `git add -A` mis-scoped a commit — the earlier lesson was recorded as 'bundles unrelated fixes', which didn't generalise to 'another agent shares this worktree'.
bugs.fix: Not rewritten: the commit was already pushed and the other session is live, so a rebase to tidy the message risks their work. Tree verified green (52 tests). Rule going forward: stage explicit paths, never `git add -A`, in any repo that may have a concurrent session; check `git status` for files this session never touched before staging.

bugs.error_message: Status line rendered 'danieldecena/home main*' while the cwd was ~/Developer/claude-spinner — the repo NAME came from one repo and the branch/dirty flag from another.
bugs.root_cause: workspace.repo describes workspace.project_dir (the directory the session started in), NOT .cwd. The two diverge as soon as a session cds into a different repo. The new owner/repo segment took .workspace.repo.name unconditionally while branch/dirty still came from `git -C $cwd`, so one segment named two different repos. Caught only because the rendered dirty marker contradicted `git status` in /Users/home, which was clean.
bugs.fix: Gate the remote on `[ "$project_dir" = "$git_root" ]` — trust workspace.repo only when project_dir IS the cwd's repo root; otherwise fall back to ${git_root##*/}, which always describes the repo git is actually being asked about.

bugs.error_message: Row columns jag: model and status start at a different x on every row
bugs.root_cause: Self-inflicted by 4a6ccb7. Sizing the name column per row (from that row's own status) fixed truncation but made the name width vary down the panel, so the model and status columns after it no longer lined up. Only visible on screen — the unit tests all passed, because each row's arithmetic was individually correct. Alignment is a property of the SET of rows, and nothing was checking the set.

bugs.error_message: buglog.json has 10 duplicate bug IDs (bug-133/134/137 from today's concurrent sessions; bug-032/072/073/092/093/095/111 older)
bugs.root_cause: IDs are allocated as max+1 from whatever the writer last read. Two Claude sessions run in this repo at once (the spinner exists to show them), so both read the same tail and both mint the same next id. Read-modify-write on one JSON file with no locking: duplicate ids are the visible damage, and a lost entry is the invisible one — if both sessions read before either writes, the first write vanishes.
bugs.fix: Fixed 2026-07-17 in .wolf/hooks/post-write.js — the OpenWolf PostToolUse auto-logger that mints ids (the same racy scheme, bugs.length+1, also lives in the global openwolf npm package; this is the project-local copy Claude Code actually runs). The read-modify-write is now serialized behind an exclusive lockfile (buglog.json.lock, O_EXCL create with a 10s stale-steal and Atomics.wait backoff); the fresh read happens INSIDE the lock; and the id is max(numeric ids)+1 — strictly above every id present, so it can never reuse one. Proven with a barrier-synchronized 20-way race test: the old length+1/no-lock pattern lost 15 of 20 concurrent writes, the locked max+1 pattern kept 20/20 with unique ids. The existing duplicate ids were left as-is (they are referenced in commits/STATUS/cerebrum; renumbering would break those references). Residual: the agent's rare manual hand-appends still bypass the lock, but the per-edit hook was the frequent collision source.

bugs.error_message: A long tool name drew two ellipses: `running askuserqu……` — the status truncated with SwiftUI's tail … and the animated working-dots rendered right after it.
bugs.root_cause: Column 3 is HStack { Text(statusLabel).truncationMode(.tail); Text(workingDots).frame(width: dotsSlot) }. When a long MCP tool name (40-50 chars) forces the shared status column to clamp below the label's width, SwiftUI truncated the label with its own …, which sat immediately before the fixed dots slot — reading as a doubled ellipsis. SwiftUI Text has no clip-without-ellipsis truncation mode, so truncationMode alone cannot avoid the glyph.
bugs.fix: Added RowLayout.fit(_:toWidth:), which pre-truncates the label in code to the column width minus statusSlack headroom (Menlo is monospaced, so the fit is exact) so SwiftUI never reaches for its tail …; the animated dots become the sole trailing signal. SessionRow.displayStatus computes the status width from the shared columns (rowFlexBudget - dotsSlot - name - model) and feeds statusLabel through fit(). Added testLongStatusLabelIsPreTruncatedToItsColumn. Verified on-screen with a throwaway long-MCP session: the long row's trailing marker is identical to the un-truncatable running-bash/thinking rows (dots only, no doubled ellipsis).
